intent: Kept a balanced first design to establish a baseline: five evenly spaced 12 mm sensors ahead of the axle, a moderate wheel track, and a light chassis. The expected result is completion on the development tracks with a moderate line-loss count, giving the Integrator a stable platform to tune. Under consideration without commitment: a wider sensor span (up to ±0.03 m) if line loss occurs at sharp bends, and a shorter forward offset (around 0.03 m) if the robot oscillates at speed. Both would be tested against this baseline.
learning: No prior races. Next iteration: compare this baseline against the Integrator's feedback on sensor span and forward offset, and use rms_error and line_loss_events to decide whether the array should widen or the sensors should move forward.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no Integration Feedback and no Geometry Race Data, so this proposal rests on design reasoning rather than evidence. The course is about 4 to 5 m and must be covered in under 3 s, so the robot needs speed (about 1.5 m/s or more) and a sensor array that reads the 25 mm tape reliably through bends. I chose five sensors at 12 mm spacing with 12 mm footprints, spanning about ±24 mm. Adjacent footprints overlap, so at least one sensor should see the tape across the line-loss-free band, and the weighted signal changes smoothly as the line moves across the array. I placed the sensors 50 mm ahead of the axle, so the robot reads the line before its wheels reach a bend, which should help high-speed stability and reduce the lag that causes overshoot. The wheel track is 0.12 m, a middle value that balances turn responsiveness against stability. The wheel radius is 0.03 m, and mass is 0.6 kg, low enough to accelerate quickly but not so light that the chassis is fragile. The body width of 0.14 m gives an off-track limit of about 0.0525 m, which is max(0.06, 0.0125+0.035), so the limit stays at 0.06 m and the track edge is not tightened. Body length is 0.16 m, which only affects the envelope. I expect a first race that completes most of the development tracks, with the main risks being overshoot on the slalom and line loss at tight bends if the Integrator's gains are too aggressive. I have not yet tested whether a wider or narrower sensor span is better, so the next iterations should compare span and forward offset.
